CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT

THIS CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT ("Agreement") is entered into effective as of May 19, 2025 (the "Effective Date"), by and between HARBORVIEW CAPITOL TOWER LLC, an affiliate of Harborview Realty Partners, LP, located at 500 Capitol Mall, Suite 1800, Sacramento, California 95814 ("Owner"), and MERIDIAN MECHANICAL GROUP, INC., a Delaware corporation d/b/a Meridian Plumbing, Heating & Air, located at 2150 Harbor Point Drive, Suite 400, Sacramento, California 95833 ("Contractor").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Owner owns real property located at 1020 J Street, Sacramento, California, commonly known as Capitol Tower (the "Building"); and

WHEREAS, Owner desires to have Contractor perform certain mechanical and plumbing work at the Building, including replacement of chiller equipment, cooling towers, and building-wide water and condenser piping systems; and

WHEREAS, Contractor is willing and able to perform such work on the terms and conditions set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, the parties agree as follows:

1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 "The Work" means all labor, materials, equipment, and services required to complete the scope of work described in Section 2 of this Agreement, including all incidental and necessary work for full and proper completion thereof in accordance with the Contract Documents.

1.2 "Contract Documents" means, collectively, this Agreement, including all Exhibits, the Specifications, the Drawings, all Addenda issued prior to execution, and any Change Orders executed after the Effective Date.

1.3 "Drawings" means the architectural and engineering drawings prepared for the Project, attached as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference.

1.4 "Specifications" means the technical specifications for the Work prepared by the Project's consulting engineers, attached as Exhibit B and incorporated herein by reference.

1.5 "Project" means the mechanical system replacement work at Capitol Tower, 1020 J Street, Sacramento, California 95814.

1.6 "Substantial Completion" means the date when the Work is sufficiently complete that Owner can occupy and utilize the Building and its mechanical systems for their intended purpose, with only minor remaining items that do not materially interfere with occupancy or operation.

1.7 "Final Completion" means the date when all remaining work, punch list items, testing, commissioning, and closeout documentation are completed to Owner's satisfaction.

1.8 "Change Order" means a written modification to the Contract Sum, Contract Time, or scope of the Work, executed by authorized representatives of both parties.

1.9 "Days" means calendar days unless otherwise specified as "Business Days."

1.10 "Project Manager" means the person designated by Owner to represent Owner's interests in day-to-day Project administration and coordination.

2. SCOPE OF WORK

2.1 Description. Contractor shall perform all work necessary to complete the replacement of two 400-ton capacity chiller units, associated cooling towers, and building-wide copper condenser piping and domestic water piping throughout Capitol Tower. The Work includes, without limitation:

2.1.1 Removal and disposal of the existing two 400-ton chillers and all cooling tower equipment;

2.1.2 Installation of two new 400-ton capacity chiller units meeting all applicable codes, standards, and performance specifications;

2.1.3 Installation of new cooling tower equipment with enhanced efficiency ratings and all associated components;

2.1.4 Complete replacement of building-wide copper condenser piping, including all necessary supports, hangers, connections, and isolation valves;

2.1.5 Complete replacement of building-wide domestic water piping using copper piping materials or such materials as specified in the Specifications;

2.1.6 Flushing, pressure testing, and certification of all piping systems in accordance with industry standards;

2.1.7 Testing, commissioning, balancing, and startup of all mechanical systems;

2.1.8 Removal of all waste, debris, and temporary facilities from the site;

2.1.9 Restoration of all areas disturbed by the Work to their original condition;

2.1.10 All labor, materials, equipment, permits as permitted by Owner, and incidental work required for proper and complete performance.

2.2 Standards and Codes. All Work shall comply with: (a) the Contract Documents; (b) the California Building Code and Sacramento Municipal Code; (c) ASHRAE standards; (d) all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations; (e) Cal/OSHA and California Department of Industrial Relations requirements; (f) all manufacturer specifications for equipment being installed; and (g) industry best practices for mechanical and plumbing contractors. In case of any conflict between the Contract Documents and applicable law, the law shall control.

2.3 Site Examination and Existing Conditions. Contractor has thoroughly examined the Project site and existing Building systems and conditions necessary to understand the difficulty and cost of performing the Work. Contractor has reviewed and verified all information contained in the Contract Documents, including drawings and specifications, and has compared such information with existing field conditions. Contractor certifies that it has examined the Building structure and layout, existing mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, occupancy and operational requirements, anticipated weather conditions, availability of labor and materials, site access and logistical constraints, and all other factors necessary to properly understand the Work. Contractor is satisfied that it possesses sufficient information to perform the Work completely and in a timely and professional manner. Contractor shall not be entitled to any additional compensation or time extension based on failure to properly examine conditions or information available at the time of inspection, except to the extent that unforeseen subsurface or concealed conditions materially differ from conditions existing at the time of Contractor's examination and were not reasonably discoverable through proper inspection and inquiry.

2.4 Regulatory Permits and Licenses. Contractor shall be responsible for obtaining all trade-specific permits and licenses required to perform the Work, including current Sacramento municipal plumbing and HVAC contractor licenses. Contractor shall maintain all licenses and permits in current, valid, and unencumbered status throughout the performance of the Work. Contractor shall cooperate with Owner regarding any permits that must be obtained by Owner from Sacramento or other governmental entities and shall provide Owner with certified copies of all permits obtained by Contractor prior to commencing any Work.

2.5 Building Occupancy and Operations. The Building is occupied and operationally active during performance of the Work. Contractor shall perform all Work in a manner that minimizes disruption to Building operations, tenant occupancy, and occupant safety. Contractor shall coordinate all work schedules with Owner's Building Manager, David Rothstein, and shall schedule any work that requires chiller shutdown, water service interruption, or other operational disruption only during hours specified by Owner, which are generally limited to evenings after 5:00 p.m., weekdays, and weekends. Contractor shall maintain all occupied spaces, common areas, and emergency access pathways in safe condition at all times and shall use plastic sheeting, temporary barriers, and other protective measures as necessary to prevent dust and debris from affecting occupants. Contractor shall maintain regular communication with Owner's facility personnel regarding work schedules and operational status.

3. CONTRACT SUM

4. TIME FOR COMPLETION

4.1 Notice to Proceed and Commencement. The Notice to Proceed date shall be June 2, 2025 (the "NTP Date"). Contractor shall not commence any Work prior to receiving written Notice to Proceed from Owner. Time is of the essence in this Agreement. Contractor acknowledges that delay in performance of the Work causes significant financial harm to Owner and that Owner's damages from delay are difficult to calculate precisely.

4.2 Substantial Completion Date. Contractor shall achieve Substantial Completion of all Work by March 31, 2026 (the "Substantial Completion Date").

4.3 Final Completion. Contractor shall complete all remaining work items, address all punch list items, perform all required testing and balancing, deliver all warranties and operations manuals, and achieve Final Completion within fourteen (14) days after Substantial Completion or as otherwise specified by Owner in writing.

4.4 Schedule. Contractor shall prepare and submit to Owner for approval a detailed Project schedule within ten (10) days of the NTP Date. The schedule shall include all major phases of work, equipment delivery dates, installation sequences, testing and commissioning activities, and all other material milestones. Contractor shall maintain and update the schedule monthly and shall provide copies to Owner. Contractor shall immediately notify Owner of any schedule delays, potential delays, or other impacts to the Substantial Completion Date.

4.5 Liquidated Damages for Delay. The parties acknowledge that failure to achieve Substantial Completion by March 31, 2026 causes significant financial and economic harm to Owner due to lost rental income, continued operating expenses, and other occupancy-related economic impacts, and that the amount of such damages is difficult to ascertain. Accordingly, the parties agree that if Contractor fails to achieve Substantial Completion by March 31, 2026, Contractor shall pay to Owner liquidated damages in the amount of two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) per day for each day of delay beyond the Substantial Completion Date, until Substantial Completion is achieved. Liquidated damages shall be deducted from progress payments due to Contractor and shall be the exclusive remedy for delay, except to the extent that delay is caused solely by Owner or by force majeure events for which Contractor has no responsibility. Contractor shall continue performing the Work throughout any delay period and shall use reasonable efforts to minimize the duration of delay.

4.6 Time Extensions. The Substantial Completion Date may only be extended by written Change Order executed by authorized representatives of both Owner and Contractor. Change Orders for time extensions shall be considered only for conditions beyond Contractor's reasonable control that cause demonstrable delays, including but not limited to: (a) unforeseen subsurface or concealed differing site conditions that Contractor could not have discovered through proper inspection; (b) acts of God or force majeure events; (c) Owner-directed changes to the scope of Work or Owner-directed delays; or (d) delays caused by other contractors or Owner's agents. Contractor shall provide Owner with detailed written notice of any claim for delay within twenty-one (21) days of the first occurrence of the delaying event, in accordance with the procedures set forth in Section 7.

5. PAYMENT AND RETAINAGE

5.1 Progress Payments. Owner shall pay Contractor for the Work on a monthly basis based upon Contractor's Application for Payment submitted in accordance with the provisions of this Section 5. Contractor shall submit applications for payment to Owner by the 20th day of each month, covering work completed through the last day of the previous month. Each Application for Payment shall include: (a) a detailed breakdown of work completed during the payment period; (b) a statement of the percentage of completion and percentage of contract value earned; (c) itemized invoices for major materials and equipment supplied during the period; (d) proof of payment to suppliers and subcontractors for prior period work; and (e) a certification by Contractor that all prior lien waivers are accurate and that all suppliers and subcontractors have been paid for work performed in prior periods.

5.2 Payment Processing and Authorization. Owner shall review each Application for Payment within seven (7) Business Days of receipt and shall approve or disapprove the application in writing. Owner shall pay approved applications within fourteen (14) days of approval, provided that no payment shall be due and payable if the Work is not progressing in accordance with the Contract schedule or if any deficiencies or non-conformities exist in the completed Work.

5.3 Retainage. Owner shall retain five percent (5%) of each progress payment until Final Completion of the Work. Upon achievement of Substantial Completion, fifty percent (50%) of the retainage accumulated to that date shall be released, provided that no apparent deficiencies or non-conformities are identified in the substantially completed Work. The remaining fifty percent (50%) of retainage shall be released within thirty (30) days after Final Completion of the Work and upon Contractor's submission of all required closeout documentation.

5.4 Final Payment. After Final Completion of all Work and upon Contractor's submission of: (a) a final Application for Payment covering all remaining work; (b) final unconditional lien waivers from Contractor and all subcontractors; (c) proof of payment to all suppliers and subcontractors in full; (d) current certificates of insurance; (e) as-built drawings; (f) all equipment warranties and operations and maintenance manuals; (g) final testing and commissioning reports; and (h) evidence of Owner's final inspection and sign-off, Owner shall pay the outstanding balance of the Contract Sum, including all accrued retainage, within thirty (30) days.

5.5 No Payment for Deficient Work. Owner shall not be obligated to pay for any portion of the Work that fails to comply with the Contract Documents, applicable law, or industry standards. If deficient or non-conforming work is discovered during inspection, Owner may: (a) require Contractor to correct the deficiency or non-conformity at Contractor's sole cost and expense; (b) withhold payment in an amount sufficient to cover the reasonable cost of correction; or (c) employ others to correct the work and deduct the actual cost of correction from amounts due to Contractor.

5.6 Lien Waivers. Contractor shall submit unconditional final lien waivers from itself and all subcontractors with each progress payment application. Failure to provide current, signed lien waivers shall result in withholding of the entire payment until waivers are received.

6. CHANGES IN THE WORK

6.1 No Extra Work Without Authorization. Contractor shall perform no work outside the scope of the Contract Documents and no changes to the Work without prior written authorization from Owner. No verbal instructions or site directions shall be deemed sufficient authorization for extra work or changes. All changes to the Work, the Contract Sum, or the Contract Time must be documented by a written Change Order executed by authorized representatives of both Owner and Contractor before any such work commences.

6.2 Change Order Request Procedures and Content. Any request by Contractor for a Change Order must include: (a) a detailed description of the proposed change or extra work; (b) the reason for the change; (c) a detailed breakdown of all costs, including labor costs, material costs, equipment rental or purchase costs, overhead allocation, and profit; (d) the proposed impact on the Contract Time, if any; (e) a schedule showing how the change will be sequenced relative to other Work; (f) identification of any materials or equipment affected by the change; (g) certification by Contractor that all cost estimates are based on current market conditions and rates; and (h) such other information as Owner reasonably requests. Owner shall review proposed Change Orders and shall respond to Contractor within fourteen (14) days with Owner's approval, conditional approval, or rejection. Owner has no obligation to approve any Change Order and retains sole and absolute discretion to reject any proposed changes.

6.3 Owner-Directed Changes. Only Owner may direct changes to the Work. Contractor shall not make any changes, modifications, substitutions, or deletions from the Contract scope without explicit written authorization from Owner in the form of a duly executed Change Order. Any work performed by Contractor without proper Owner authorization shall be performed entirely at Contractor's cost and expense with no adjustment to the Contract Sum or Contract Time.

6.4 Pricing of Changes. Costs for Owner-approved changes shall be calculated and charged based on: (a) the fixed rates established in the original bid or quotation for the Work; (b) actual costs incurred plus fifteen percent (15%) markup for overhead and profit; or (c) such other basis as Owner and Contractor mutually agree upon in writing. Owner shall not approve any single Change Order that increases the Contract Sum by more than five percent (5%) without additional review and authorization by Owner's board.

6.5 Time Impact of Changes. Any Change Order that impacts the Substantial Completion Date shall specify the revised Substantial Completion Date. Time extensions shall be granted only to the extent necessary to accommodate the additional or changed Work in a manner consistent with good scheduling practices, and no time extension shall be granted for delays caused by Contractor's inefficiency, inability to properly manage or coordinate the change with existing work, or delays that could have been avoided by reasonable foresight.

7. CLAIMS AND DISPUTES

7.1 Notice of Claims. Contractor shall provide Owner with written notice of any and all claims for additional compensation, time extensions, or any other relief or remedy within twenty-one (21) days of the date upon which the event or condition giving rise to the claim first occurs. Failure to provide written notice within this twenty-one-day period shall result in waiver of the claim except to the extent that Owner had actual knowledge of the event or condition.

7.2 Claim Notice Content. Each claim notice shall include: (a) a detailed description of the event, condition, or circumstance giving rise to the claim; (b) the specific date upon which the event occurred; (c) reference to the specific provision of the Contract Documents or fact giving rise to the claim; (d) all supporting documentation, including photographs, test reports, correspondence, and other evidence; (e) calculation of damages or additional costs claimed, if applicable; and (f) description of any mitigation efforts undertaken.

7.3 Detailed Claim Submission. Within fourteen (14) days after providing initial notice, Contractor shall submit a detailed, fully documented claim in writing to Owner. The claim shall include all documentation, cost substantiation, calculations, analysis, and supporting evidence necessary for Owner to fully evaluate and understand the claim. Claims submitted after the fourteen-day period shall not be considered or evaluated unless Owner agrees in writing to extend the deadline.

7.4 Owner's Review and Response. Owner shall review all submitted claims and shall provide Contractor with written notice of Owner's position within fourteen (14) days of receipt. If Owner requires additional information or clarification, Owner shall notify Contractor of the deficiencies or gaps, and Contractor shall have seven (7) days to provide the requested information. If Contractor fails or refuses to provide requested information within the seven-day period, the claim shall be deemed denied.

7.5 Payment for Approved Claims. If Owner determines that a claim is valid and supported by the Contract Documents, applicable law, or industry standards, Owner shall process payment for the claim through the next available progress payment application. Approval of a claim does not constitute a waiver of any other rights, claims, or remedies that Owner may have.

7.6 Binding Arbitration. Any dispute, claim, or controversy arising out of or related to this Agreement, the Work, the Project, or the relationship between Owner and Contractor, which cannot be resolved through good faith negotiation and the claim procedures set forth in this Section 7, shall be resolved by binding arbitration administered by JAMS (Judicial Arbitration and Mediation Services) under the JAMS Construction Arbitration Rules & Procedures then in effect. The arbitration shall be conducted before a single arbitrator mutually selected by the parties, or, if no mutual selection is reached within thirty (30) days, an arbitrator appointed by JAMS. The arbitration shall be conducted in Sacramento, California. The arbitrator shall apply California law and shall issue a written decision and award explaining the factual and legal basis for the award. The costs and fees of arbitration shall be shared equally by the parties unless the arbitrator awards costs and fees to the prevailing party.

8. INSURANCE AND BONDS

8.1 Performance and Payment Bond. Prior to commencing any Work, Contractor shall provide Owner with a Performance and Payment Bond in the penal sum equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the Contract Sum. The bond shall be issued by a surety company licensed to do business in California and rated at least A- by A.M. Best. The bond shall be on an AIA form A311 or such other form as Owner approves in writing. The Performance Bond shall guarantee the faithful performance of all terms and conditions of this Agreement, and the Payment Bond shall guarantee payment of all labor, materials, equipment, and other costs of the Work. Contractor shall provide evidence of the bond to Owner prior to receiving the Notice to Proceed and prior to commencing any Work.

8.2 Comprehensive General Liability Insurance. Contractor shall obtain and maintain, at Contractor's sole expense, comprehensive general liability insurance with minimum limits of not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence and two million dollars ($2,000,000) annual aggregate. Contractor shall also obtain and maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by California law, property insurance on all equipment and materials on site, and such other insurance as may be required by law or prudent industry practice. All insurance policies shall name Owner as an additional insured and shall provide that coverage is primary and non-contributory with respect to any insurance carried by Owner. All policies shall include a provision requiring that the issuing insurance company notify Owner at least thirty (30) days prior to cancellation or material modification.

8.3 Insurance Certificates and Documentation. Contractor shall provide Owner with certificates of insurance for all required policies prior to commencing Work and shall provide updated certificates at least annually during the course of the Work and prior to final payment. Each certificate shall include a statement that the issuing insurance company will provide Owner at least thirty (30) days' written notice prior to cancellation, non-renewal, or material modification of any policy.

8.4 Notice of Loss or Incident. Contractor shall immediately notify Owner in writing of any loss, damage, accident, or incident that could result in a claim against any of the insurance policies maintained under this Agreement.

8.5 No Limitation of Liability. Contractor's maintenance of insurance and bonds shall not limit or reduce Contractor's liability or responsibility under this Agreement, nor shall it be deemed a waiver of Owner's rights to recover damages from Contractor for breach of contract or negligence beyond the limits of the insurance policies maintained.

9. WARRANTY

9.1 Warranty of Work Quality. Contractor warrants that all Work will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner and in full compliance with the Contract Documents, industry standards, and all applicable law. Contractor warrants that all materials and equipment supplied or installed by Contractor shall be of high quality, free from defects in material and workmanship, and fit for their intended purpose.

9.2 Duration of Warranty. Contractor's warranty shall extend for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of Substantial Completion. Contractor shall promptly correct any defective or non-conforming work discovered during the warranty period at no additional cost to Owner. Contractor shall be responsible for all costs associated with removal and replacement of defective work, including labor costs, material costs, disposal costs, and any damage caused by the correction process.

9.3 Manufacturer's Warranties and Registration. Contractor shall transfer to Owner all manufacturer warranties for equipment and materials supplied or incorporated into the Work. Contractor shall work with equipment manufacturers to ensure that warranties are properly registered and that Owner receives all warranty documents, registration confirmations, and instructions for making warranty claims.

9.4 Extended Equipment Warranties. For all chiller and cooling tower equipment installed as part of the Work, Contractor shall either: (a) obtain from the manufacturer and assign to Owner an extended warranty covering parts and labor for a minimum of five (5) years from the date of system startup; or (b) provide Owner with documentation demonstrating that such extended warranties are included with the equipment. The cost of any extended warranties shall be included in the Contract Sum with no additional charge.

10. INDEMNIFICATION

10.1 Indemnity by Contractor. Contractor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Owner, its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against all claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees and costs of defense, arising out of or resulting from: (a) Contractor's performance or failure to perform the Work; (b) any breach of this Agreement by Contractor; (c) any negligence or willful misconduct by Contractor or its agents, employees, or subcontractors; (d) bodily injury or property damage caused by the Work or Contractor's operations; (e) Contractor's violation of any law or regulation; (f) liens, claims, or encumbrances filed against the Property by Contractor or its suppliers, subcontractors, or agents; or (g) any defective, non-conforming, or non-compliant Work.

10.2 Defense of Third-Party Claims. Contractor shall defend Owner against any third-party claims arising out of the matters covered by Section 10.1 using counsel approved by Owner. Contractor shall not settle any claim without Owner's prior written consent.

10.3 Exclusive Remedy. Contractor's obligation to indemnify Owner shall be Contractor's sole and exclusive remedy for claims arising out of the Work, and Contractor waives any right to contribution or indemnification from Owner for such claims.

11. GENERAL PROVISIONS

11.1 Safety and Compliance. Contractor is responsible for the safety of all Work performed and for the safety of Contractor's employees, agents, subcontractors, and any other persons present on the Project site due to Contractor's operations. Contractor shall comply with all Cal/OSHA requirements and shall implement all safety procedures and protocols required by law or prudent industry practice. Contractor shall maintain a current written injury prevention plan and shall make such plan available to Owner upon request.

11.2 Site Conditions and Cleanup. Contractor shall keep the Project site in a clean and orderly condition at all times during performance of the Work. Contractor shall remove trash, waste, and debris from the site daily and shall dispose of same in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental laws. Upon completion of all Work, Contractor shall remove all temporary facilities, equipment, and materials from the site and shall restore the site to its original condition.

11.3 Coordination with Owner and Other Contractors. Contractor shall coordinate its work schedule with Owner and any other contractors or trades working at the Building. Contractor shall attend weekly project coordination meetings with Owner or Owner's representatives and shall provide advance notice of any work activities that may impact Building operations or other contractors.

11.4 Permits and Inspections. Contractor shall be responsible for obtaining and paying for all trade-specific permits required for the Work. Owner shall be responsible for obtaining any general construction permits required from Sacramento. Contractor shall arrange and pay for all required inspections by building officials and code enforcement agencies and shall promptly correct any deficiencies or non-conformities noted during inspections.

11.5 Protection of Existing Work and Property. Contractor shall protect all existing Building systems, structures, finishes, and adjacent property from damage during performance of the Work. Any damage to existing elements caused by Contractor's negligence or improper work shall be repaired by Contractor at Contractor's sole cost and expense.

11.6 Material Quality and Testing. All materials and equipment shall meet or exceed the quality standards specified in the Specifications. All materials and equipment shall be new unless otherwise specified in the Contract Documents. Contractor shall arrange and pay for all required testing and certification of materials, systems, and installations, including but not limited to pressure testing of piping systems, startup testing and commissioning of mechanical equipment, and such other testing as required by law or the Contract Documents.

11.7 Warranty Registration and Documentation. Contractor shall be responsible for registering all equipment warranties with manufacturers and shall provide Owner with all warranty documentation, including warranty certificates, registration confirmations, and instructions for making warranty claims.

11.8 Final Inspection and Acceptance. Owner shall conduct a final inspection of the Work prior to Final Completion. Contractor shall not claim Final Completion until all items on Owner's punch list have been corrected to Owner's reasonable satisfaction. Owner's final inspection and sign-off shall be conclusive evidence of the quality and completion of the Work.

12. GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION

12.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

12.2 Exclusive Venue and Jurisdiction. The parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in Sacramento County, California for resolution of any disputes arising under this Agreement.

12.3 Waiver of Jury Trial. The parties waive any right to jury trial in connection with any dispute arising under this Agreement.

12.4 Attorneys' Fees. In any proceeding to enforce this Agreement or resolve disputes between the parties, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys' fees and costs, including expert fees and costs of investigation, from the other party.

13. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

13.1 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with the Contract Documents, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties regarding the Work and the Project and supersedes all prior negotiations, understandings, and agreements. No modification or amendment shall be effective unless in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

13.2 Order of Precedence. In the event of any conflict or ambiguity between or among the documents comprising the Contract Documents, the order of precedence shall be: (1) this Agreement; (2) any executed Change Orders in reverse chronological order; (3) the Specifications (Exhibit B); (4) the Drawings (Exhibit A); and (5) any other referenced documents.

13.3 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is determined to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect, and the invalid provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid and enforceable.

13.4 Waiver. No waiver of any breach or provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party against whom the waiver is sought. Waiver of any breach shall not constitute waiver of any subsequent breach or any other provision.

13.5 Assignment. Neither party shall assign any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party. Any attempted assignment without consent shall be void.

13.6 Notices. Any notice required under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be delivered personally, sent by overnight courier service, or sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the addresses set forth in the signature blocks below. Notice shall be deemed effective upon receipt.

13.7 Successors and Assigns. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors and assigns, except that neither party may assign without consent as provided in Section 13.5.

13.8 Independent Contractor Status. Contractor is an independent contractor. Nothing in this Agreement creates an employment relationship, partnership, joint venture, or agency relationship between the parties. Contractor is responsible for paying all employment taxes, workers' compensation insurance, and providing all employment-related benefits to Contractor's employees.

13.9 Authority and Representations. Each party represents and warrants that it has full authority to enter into this Agreement and that the person executing this Agreement on its behalf is duly authorized to do so.

13.10 Counterparts and Electronic Execution. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery by facsimile or PDF shall have the same force and effect as delivery of manually executed originals.

13.11 Calculation of Time. Unless otherwise specified as "Business Days," all references to days in this Agreement shall mean calendar days. If any deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, the deadline shall be extended to the next Business Day.
